question: A squadron that came from a scene row had an empty +3D0h member array when GameAiCoordinatorHost::Impl::build_squadrons asked, so every wingman seeded an AI squadron of its own: USN04 built 7 over 15 where the mission has 5. Find why and fix it so every consumer sees a resolved array.
answer: The resolver existed and ran too late. GameScriptOrdersHost::resolve_plane_squadron_members fills the registry's +3D0h array by name for scene rows and launches alike, but its only call sites were in the mission loop, while build_squadrons runs from create_units' tail via host.ai->create_00a32350(). The header advertised the resolver as `resolve_member_units`, a name that exists nowhere, which is why a grep for it came back empty and a duplicate got written before the real one was found. The body needed nothing from the scripts-orders host - only the process-wide plane_squadron_registry() and the units host's own count()/unit_row() - so it became a free function, bsp::game::resolve_plane_squadron_members(units, log, only_unresolved), with the member as a one-line delegate, and create_units calls it after the slots exist and before the AI host is constructed. The find_by_member_name fallback added while this was being chased is removed in the same commit, leaving one route.
coverage: complete for the scene route: measured. NOT complete for the air-ops route, which is a separate ordering defect this packet located but did not fix.

the torpedo release-order broadcast that reads the same array through find_by_member_unit; it saw zero members for a scene-row squadron before this

corrections.evidence: `resolve_member_units` appears in that one comment and nowhere else in src/ or include/; the real name has two mission-loop call sites.

corrections.was: The same header said member_units is filled 'by the units host'.
corrections.is: It was filled inline by the air-ops route only, and by the resolver for everything else. After this commit the units host does fill it, so the line is true as written for the first time.
corrections.evidence: game_hosts_script_orders.cpp pushes member_units per wing at launch; the scene path in game_hosts_scene_contents.cpp clears it and fills only member_names and member_spawn_index.

corrections.was: A registry-level resolve_member_units written by this packet.
corrections.is: Deleted as a duplicate; the existing body is the one implementation, and its preserve-filled-slots behaviour was dropped as an unnecessary extra rule since 007F4B55 keys the array on the names.
corrections.evidence: Both did the same job; the existing one has the run record behind it.

validation: Build clean at /W4 /WX, both ctest suites pass, and it links. Three runs on the final binary. USN01: 'plane squadron members: 5 of 5 wing record(s) resolved to units over 5 squadron(s)' at create_units time, before the AI host exists, so find_by_member_unit answers Mav1's record from then on and 007EEF30 sees live members. USN01: 'ai squadron wing_count +3C8h=1 over 5 squadron(s)', so the filter takes the AUTHORED WingCount rather than 007F4735's absent-key default of 3; USN04 cannot discriminate this because authored and default coincide at 3 there. USN04: first census 1 squadron over 3 member planes, which is what the removed fallback used to produce, so removing it cost nothing.
open: USN04 still ends at 7 squadrons over 15 planes. The progression 1/3, 4/6, 5/9, 6/12, 7/15 says the FIRST air-ops launch adds three planes as three squadrons while every later launch adds three as one. The ungrouped diagnostic printed no line, and it prints only when find_by_member_name succeeds, so the registry does not know those planes by name when the census runs: the record is not there yet rather than there and wrong. Reading eliminated the other two candidates - the wing name goes into both the unit record and member_names from the same expression, and member_units[wing] = before + wing matches batch order. Caveat: an unnamed unit would produce the same silence, and separating that needs the plane's name in the diagnostic line.
